title: A 12-Inch Sea Bug Sat Unnoticed in a University for 40 Years

scenes.text: A 12-inch sea bug sat in a university collection for 40 years.
It's a giant isopod, a deep-sea cousin of the little pill bug in your garden.
A professor bought it in Puerto Rico in the 1980s, and it was filed away.
Then a student looked closer and realised it was a species nobody had named.
It's 12.7 inches long, and just got its name this month.
Forty years in a drawer. A brand new species.

description:
A giant isopod bought in Puerto Rico in the 1980s sat in the University of Tübingen's collection for about 40 years until a student recognised it as a new species.
It measures about 12.7 inches and was published in Scientific Reports in October 2026.
What do you think is sitting unnoticed in other collections?

first_comment: Bonus: its name honors both Tübingen and Puerto Rico's native name, Borikén. Would you hold one?
